title: Resi4Rent — Website Redesign
desc: A rental website rebuilt around finding a place

blocks.title: Resi4Rent — Website Redesign
blocks.lede: Rebuilding a rental website around the one thing that actually matters: finding a place.

items.label: Role
items.value: UX research, information architecture, UX/UI, art direction, web design

items.label: Scope
items.value: Research, personas, IA, desktop, mobile, design system

items.statement: The site wasn’t short on information. It was short on direction.
body: Resi4Rent was already a major name in the Polish rental market, but the website made the process feel more complicated than it needed to be.

blocks.statement: Research made the problem hard to ignore.

items.description: didn’t know how to move from browsing to contacting an agent.
said the visuals didn’t give them enough confidence to act.

body: There was no meaningful analytics setup either, so the business couldn’t clearly see where people were dropping out.

I started with surveys, interviews, analytics, heuristic review and competitor benchmarking. A five-whys analysis of contact abandonment took us past “the CTA is unclear” to the bigger problem: the site was organised around the company, not the user’s decision.
So the core journey became: City → Area → Apartment → Contact.

blocks.text: The best advert for a rental subscription is a website where you can actually find one.

body: Search became the main interface. The neighbourhood map became part of the browsing experience instead of an afterthought. Mobile was redesigned as a real product experience, not simply a smaller desktop layout.
Filters, distance-to-amenities, the application flow and trust signals were all rebuilt around the same idea: make the next step obvious.
Everything was backed by a mobile-first design system built to scale as the service expanded.

blocks.statement: The research told us where the friction was. The redesign removed it.
body: The route from homepage to contacting an agent became a clear four-step journey instead of a collection of disconnected pages.
